docs.text: Pizza BFO Ontology A pizza ontology aligned to BFO 2020 - the BFO that NFDIcore 3.0.5 builds on - and made from BFO and NFDIcore design patterns. It holds no individuals: its instance data is a separate knowledge graph built from ROBOT templates. This site is published from the docs/ folder of this repository by GitHub Actions, every time main changes. Getting the ontology What Where Browse https://ebrahimnorouzi.github.io/pizza-bfo/pizzabfo.owl Edit file src/ontology/pizzabfo-edit.owl Released file pizzabfo.owl Documentation The ontology's documentation page Edit the edit file , never the released one: the released file is produced by the build and is overwritten by it. Turning this site on GitHub does not publish Pages until it is asked. Once, in the repository's Settings > Pages , set the source to Deploy from a branch and choose the gh-pages branch - the workflow creates that branch the first time it runs. The site then appears at https://<owner>.github.io/<repository>/ .

docs.text: Editing Pizza BFO Ontology With Protege and OntoBoard Open src/ontology/pizzabfo-edit.owl . Work on the OntoBoard tab, or in Protege's own views. Run OntoBoard > Project > Build... and choose test before you commit. It runs the same checks the repository's CI runs. Identifiers New terms are minted from the range allocated to you in src/ontology/pizzabfo-idranges.owl . Give each editor their own range - OntoBoard > Project > ID ranges... - so two people never mint the same identifier for different things. docs.text: Releasing Pizza BFO Ontology A release is a frozen copy that other ontologies can import and that will not change under them. This project numbers its releases semantically: MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH . Make sure test passes: OntoBoard > Build and release > Build... , target test . OntoBoard > Build and release > Release... , Semantic version , the next version. It stamps the version IRI https://ebrahimnorouzi.github.io/pizza-bfo/pizzabfo/<version> , with owl:versionInfo and owl:priorVersion , and writes releases/<version>/pizzabfo.owl and the published pizzabfo.owl . Publish the release under its IRIs: copy pizzabfo.owl to docs/pizzabfo.owl , and releases/<version>/pizzabfo.owl to docs/pizzabfo/<version> - with no extension, as in the version IRI. This site serves them at those addresses. OntoBoard > Build and release > Documentation... , Write it to docs/ontology , Include the WebVowl diagram ticked. It documents the release you just made, and its changelog compares that release with the one before it - which has to be online already, as step 3 of the last release put it. Commit all of it, tag the commit v<version> , and push. This site is republished from main . The knowledge graph in kg/ has releases of its own, under kg/releases/ . A version IRI cannot be taken back once somebody has imported it, so the release step refuses to overwrite a release that already exists.

docs.text: Requirements (eXtreme Design scoping) Written before modelling. Each iteration takes one or two stories, finds the design pattern that answers them, and ends in a release. Principles Aligned to BFO 2020 , the version of the Basic Formal Ontology that NFDIcore 3.0.5 uses (its entity , material entity , quality , role , process , one-dimensional temporal region and the 2020 relations such as has continuant part ). Patterns, not invention : the BFO and NFDIcore patterns bundled with OntoBoard. No individuals in the ontology. It says what pizzas, toppings, bakers and bakings are . Which pizzas a pizzeria actually sells and bakes is instance data: a separate knowledge graph, filled from ROBOT templates ( kg/ ), that imports the ontology. User stories Story S1 As a menu planner, I want to describe a pizza by its base and toppings, so that menus can be compared. S2 As a guest, I want to know which pizzas are spicy, so that I can avoid or choose them. S3 As a pizzeria, I want to record who baked a pizza, in which oven and when, so that orders can be traced. S4 As a data steward, I want the pizzeria's menu and bakings recorded as data, not in the ontology, so that the ontology stays reusable. Competency questions Question Story Iteration CQ1 What parts does a pizza have - its base and its toppings? S1 1 CQ2 Which toppings does each named pizza have? S1 1 CQ3 Which pizzas are cheesy, and which have meat? S1 1 CQ4 Which toppings are hot, and so which pizzas are spicy? S2 2 CQ5 Who baked a given pizza, in which oven, and over which period? S3 3 CQ6 Which role does a baker realize in a baking? S3 3 CQ7 Which pizzas did a pizzeria bake on a given day? (answered by the knowledge graph) S4 KG Contextual statements A pizza is an object (BFO); its base is a fiat object part of it and its toppings are material entity parts - related with BFO 2020's has continuant part . Spiciness is a quality that inheres in a topping; a topping is its bearer . Baking a pizza is a process that realizes a baker role , occurs in an oven and occupies a one-dimensional temporal region; the role is the role of an agent. Reasoning requirements A pizza with a cheese topping is a cheesy pizza ; with a meat topping, a meaty pizza . A topping that bears a hot spiciness is a spicy topping , and a pizza that has one is a spicy pizza - found by the reasoner, never asserted. The ontology must stay in OWL 2 EL, so ELK classifies it.
docs.title: Requirements (eXtreme Design scoping)
